title: Persist stable saved-TV identity without merging or deleting devices on weak address evidence
description: Remaining so-fb3.1 scope after accepted .1.1 truthful discovery rows: mobile saved-device persistence (v2/mobile/src/lib/savedDevices.ts) currently (a) matches a saved row by host alone when either side lacks a hardware id, transferring cached name/type on IP-only evidence; (b) rememberDevice deletes any other saved row that still claims the same host but has a different hardware id (host set to empty then filtered), destroying that TV's history on DHCP address reuse; (c) forgetDevice removes every row at host:port regardless of identity; (d) cachedDeviceName returns the first row at a host even when rows with different ids share it. Pure node:test fixtures cover: mixed saved/new, duplicate advertisements, address and port change with same id, id conflict at same address, missing id on either side, cancellation/stale-response independence (pure functions only), MAX truncation and lastUsed ordering. title: Preserve launcher failure stages and verify rollback reporting
description:
Bounded implementation for GitHub #87: launcher failure and rollback handling. This fixes source-proven defects in the reported error path; it is not a claim to reproduce or resolve the Sony firmware behavior.

Owner: existing serial Sol high implementation helper under Mayor/Flowkeeper. Mechanic architecture/final acceptance; Navigator independent source/copy review. Source-only candidate stage in this capsule first. Only candidate/v2/crates/core/src/commands/launcher.rs may change, including its colocated tests. Original inputs and all preserved app/candidate workspaces stay frozen. Parent so-x02 stays open for actual Sony switching evidence. No new worker/runtime/worktree/install.

Confirmed source facts at baseline 48cba2384ca3938e6655b77ccf85716dd86cca5f:
1. Both frontend row actions call the same setDefaultLauncher(pkg). Rust always attempts pm enable target; a real disabled->enabled device transition can change HOME but there is no separate frontend implementation. That possible device state difference is not root-cause proof.
2. set_default_launcher_impl ignores initial target-enable transport and reported shell failures, then continues toward stock takeover.
3. stock_takeover checks its disable output only into disabled_ok. If false, it skips HOME verification AND restoration and emits the same 'Disabled ... so it was re-enabled' error. A transport error also cannot prove the disable had no effect.
4. After an unverified successful disable it attempts pm enable stock but ignores the result, emits the same success-sounding restoration claim, and returns the stale pre-operation HOME package.
5. AOSP Android 8 supports set-home-activity and query-activities. Do not add a speculative pm fallback or claim Android 8 lacks these APIs. Reference: https://android.googlesource.com/platform/frameworks/base/+/android-8.0.0_r4/services/core/java/com/android/server/pm/PackageManagerShellCommand.java .

Required behavior:
- Handle target pm enable failures before any role/setter/HOME/stock-disable work. Both transport failure and unsuccessful returned output (exit status and existing both-stream shell_reported_failure seam) return a stage-specific false result with diagnostic context. Do not disable/re-enable the target as a workaround.
- Keep the current stock-catalog-only restriction, package validation, never-disable classification, and explicit allow_stock_disable gate. Keep normal successful strategy behavior and verified takeover results unchanged. No global classifier, catalog, frontend or API schema edits.
- Once a stock-disable command has been issued, any outcome other than verified target HOME must attempt restoring that same previously active stock package. This includes rejected/error/indeterminate disable results: the call may have had an effect before transport failure. Skip HOME intent/target verification on a known disable-command failure, but do not skip restoration. Do not change unrelated packages. Successful verified takeover must not be undone.
- Report the actual failure stage: target enable, stock disable, or takeover verification. Preserve useful primary error context. Distinguish restoration command failure from command acknowledgement. A clean command result supports 'restore command completed', not verified enabled-state proof; avoid claiming 'was re-enabled' unless separately verified. Do not hide the original failure behind a cleanup failure.
- After a restore attempt obtain a fresh HOME observation for current_launcher; return None when unavailable. Never substitute the original stock string for a failed final query. The error must remain truthful even if the final HOME resolver reports a different package or no result.
- Keep Result<SetLauncherResult,String>, fields, and pure engine unchanged. Helper functions inside this same module are allowed if they simplify stage-specific results. No broader strategy-ladder, timing/backoff, resolver-format or device-discovery redesign.

Implementation tests: use existing MockAdb command logs/sequences and small test-only stubs INSIDE launcher.rs as needed for stderr/nonzero/unknown output. Do not edit shared commands/mod.rs: #88 owns a pending accepted mock logging change there. No second production ADB wrapper. Tests must assert actual ordered commands and result fields, not only string snapshots.

Validation allowed automatically: source whitelist/hashes, rustfmt, focused launcher Rust synthetic tests single process/--test-threads=1 in a disposable offline fixture with bounded disk and no real devices/network. If the fixture cannot build offline within host limits, report the exact missing dependency/gate; do not install or launch full Tauri. No heavy full app build, GUI/browser/gallery/performance. Return frozen diff.patch, hashes.json, handoff.txt, actual test names/results/platform and outstanding gates. No commits/pushes/releases, device/SSH/ADB execution, permissions/global settings/daemon mutation. Routine corrections through the same serial helper only.
acceptance_criteria:
Focused behavioral contract:
A. Invalid package: no commands, false result.
B. Target enable transport failure, stdout shell failure, stderr shell failure, and nonzero/unknown returned status: no role, setter, HOME kick or stock disable; stage-specific failure, no fabricated current launcher. An already enabled target with a valid acknowledgement retains existing path.
C. Protected stock, non-stock active, or opt-out: never disable it; no restore command without an issued stock-disable call.
D. Stock disable transport failure and reported failure: restore same stock attempted exactly once, no HOME kick, result distinguishes disable failure, no unobserved restored claim.
E. Stock disable acknowledged but target never verifies: existing HOME kick and bounded polls then one restore; error distinguishes verification failure and actual restore outcome.
F. Restore transport/nonzero/stdout/stderr failure: false result keeps primary failure plus restoration failure; never says restored/re-enabled successfully. Final resolver failure produces None, final different observed HOME is returned as observed.
G. Acknowledged restore with unavailable HOME: false result describes completed command without claiming observed enabled/current state; None current_launcher.
H. Verified takeover: true disable_stock_takeover, target current_launcher, no rollback; existing role/set-home successful fast-path behavior retained.
I. No target disable command, no extra packages affected, no never-disable/caution rule changes; only owned launcher.rs changes.
J. Exact frozen-source Navigator review before local integration. This focused failure-path milestone does not close parent Sony issue; reporter/device controlled failure-vs-success HOME outputs remain a separate gate.
notes:
Navigator independent CONTRACT ACCEPTANCE at manifest e83af3ce6ff194fe7563cbb157a48818e16e3fd2d29a1a29bf50500b00ddf324. Manifest, brief, acceptance and all seven original pins match; candidate launcher.rs is still byte-identical to original SHA256 85ac26f550f90cf07629fc323624a5eb0421863cf7009eeb747e2b67f7ca1894, so this is contract review only, not frozen-delta source acceptance. Accepted mandatory safety nuance: after any issued stock-disable whose target takeover is not verified, attempt exactly one restore of the same prior stock package even when disable returned transport/reported failure, because effect is indeterminate; known disable failure skips HOME kick/polls but not restore. Initial target-enable failure aborts before role/setter/HOME/stock work. Stage-specific primary error remains visible alongside restore outcome; clean restore command completion does not prove enabled/active state; final current_launcher comes only from a fresh resolver and is None when unavailable. Copy precision: say Android/the TV reports X as the Home app, not that X is currently visible on screen. Contract preserves package validation, stock-only and NEVER_DISABLE checks, explicit opt-in, successful ladder/takeover behavior, schema/frontend, and parent Sony evidence gate. Acceptance matrix adequately covers transport, exit status, stdout/stderr shell markers, command order, exactly-once rollback and no false verbs/state. Next Navigator action is exact frozen launcher.rs delta review; no source edits/tests/runtime in this acceptance.
CLARIFICATION: restore command outcome and final HOME resolver outcome are independent. A failed/unknown rollback does not imply current_launcher=None; preserve any successful fresh final resolver observation, including stock, target or a third package. Return None only when that resolver observation itself is unavailable. Likewise an acknowledged restore does not prove which HOME app the independent resolver will report. This supersedes any earlier shorthand tying rollback failure to unavailable current HOME.
close_reason: Focused launcher failure/restore source correction accepted and integrated locally at 4941bf4; 26 focused tests passed, final changes comment-only. Parent so-x02 remains open for Sony physical evidence and publication.

title: Migrate desktop app and optimizer consumers to canonical Unknown safety
description:
dispatched_by: mayor
no_merge: true
merge_strategy: local

so-fb3.2.3 — bounded desktop consumer migration after mobile .2.2

Source contract prepared by Mechanic while the existing serial helper's mobile handoff is outstanding. Flowkeeper alone assigns the SAME Sol-high collaboration helper after the mobile slice's acceptance; this is not authorization for another worker or concurrent candidate edits. Mechanic owns technical decisions/frozen-source checks; Navigator owns independent source/copy acceptance. No clone/worktree, service/session startup, install, network/device operation, commit/push/release or heavy frontend build. Source capsule stays under 1 MiB.

EXACT SOURCE SCOPE
Only four existing files under candidate/ are writable:
1. v2/src/routes/devices/[serial]/+page.svelte
2. v2/src/lib/components/OptimizeTab.svelte
3. v2/src/lib/components/AppRow.svelte
4. v2/src/lib/demo-mock.ts
No new application file. handoff.txt, hashes.json and diff.patch at capsule root are allowed. original/ and all earlier candidates, acceptance records and application workspaces are immutable. manifest.json pins each source and distinguishes the four read-only accepted .2.1 contract-foundation files from the current HEAD48cba23 desktop inputs. The mobile discovery/navigation foundation and all .2.2 files are outside this scope. Do not modify shared Safety/types/API, backend commands, protection lists, StateBadge, launcher/snapshot workflows, global theme or mobile files.

SOURCE FINDINGS THIS SLICE MUST COVER
- loadHealth catches safetyInfo rejection into Safe; safeDisableFromMemory has another catch-to-Safe; memory rows substitute Safe for a missing map entry. Remove all three.
- fetchAppStates catches package-state lookup failure by returning Enabled for every requested catalog entry. Several row/filter defaults also assume Enabled when a state is absent. An unavailable inventory is not evidence of installation or enabled state.
- Catalog disableApp/uninstallApp and Other installed apps disableOther/uninstallOther dispatch directly; both pairs require current installed-target and canonical warning guards, including direct handler calls. applyRecommendation must pass through the same guard.
- Desktop OptimizeTab currently has no safetyInfo lookup, auto-selects from catalog flags and recalculates actions against mutable props while running. It needs the canonical boundary and a frozen run.
- AppRow prints catalog risk.toUpperCase(), allowing SAFE to contradict canonical Caution/Unknown. Other-app and memory renderers also need honest labels/readiness.
- demo-mock safety_info always returns Safe, including protected examples.

CANONICAL LABELS AND INVENTORY
Use the accepted shared Safety union and validated api.safetyInfo only: Protected (never_disable), Caution, Unknown, each with its reason. Unknown is neutral, never green Safe or an automatic recommendation. Pending/rejected/invalid lookup means Checking safety or Safety unavailable, distinct from successful Unknown. No Optional evidence, package classifier, prefix heuristic or promotion from catalog risk/default flags/known name. Preserve known purpose/description separately from uncertainty about removal effects.

Keep inventory state unavailable on failure/missing or invalid response entries; do not substitute Enabled or Missing. Propagate the failure to a visible retry and disable relevant action controls. For a catalog app, current confirmed enabled/disabled state is required for removal; a catalog entry alone proves no installation. OtherPackage must come from a successful current installed-list result. Preserve source distinction so a same-named catalog row cannot validate an old OtherPackage or vice versa. AppRow may locally accept an unknown/unavailable state and render its own neutral placeholder while calling unchanged StateBadge only for its supported enabled/disabled/missing states. Do not expand shared state types or alter StateBadge solely for this fallback.
loadDevice, loadApps/packageStates, loadOtherPackages, loadHealth and safety/enrichment lookups touched here must capture serial + local page/request generation. A route reset, superseding load, observed disconnect/reload or destroy retires pending confirmations/readiness. Stale completion/error/finally must not replace the current device, readiness, rows or busy flags. Desktop has no mobile Session.generation; use a small page-local epoch and existing reset/lifecycle boundaries, pass that observed context to OptimizeTab if needed within these two owned files. Do not invent a hardware identity or claim detection of an unobserved external same-address reconnect. That broader identity issue stays open.

ALL APP-LIST REMOVAL HANDLERS
Use one page-local removal flow for catalog and other installed app Disable/Uninstall. Before offering a confirmation, capture action, package, serial, page/inventory/request tokens and current installed provenance; use existing packageStates for fresh target-state evidence when needed. Read canonical safetyInfo. Protected refuses with reason; pending/unavailable/invalid target refuses with retry; Unknown and Caution require explicit confirmation displaying the exact package/action/current reason. Existing synchronous confirm is fine; no new dialog framework or UI redesign.
After confirmation, revalidate the captured context and fetch the current canonical verdict before dispatch. A failed/protected/changed kind-or-reason result aborts; a changed warning needs a fresh user review. Do not silently capture a new serial/row after an old dialog. No optimistic state mutation precedes validation. Dispatch exactly once through the existing api.disablePackage/uninstallPackage for the captured target, and publish result/cache/message/busy updates only to the same still-current operation. Preserve entitlement/backend refusal and installed list synchronization. Direct disableOther/uninstallOther/disableApp/uninstallApp/applyRecommendation invocations must obey these rules even if a caller bypasses the button's disabled attribute.
Enable and reinstall retain their non-removal behavior with current target/context checks; they must not be blocked just because removal safety is unavailable. Reinstall of a known missing catalog package does not require pretending it is installed. Do not add ADB subprocess paths or modify launcher/snapshot/backup/clone logic. Unknown catalog entries may offer an explicit review action but must not be styled/called automatically recommended merely because default_optimize is true.

MEMORY IS INSPECT-ONLY UNTIL TYPED ATTRIBUTION
Current MemoryEntry.package may already be truncated by the backend. Display exactly the supplied field, mark its identity unverified, retain measured PSS, and never describe it as a reconstructed full/raw process identifier. Existing catalog descriptions are secondary hints, not identity proof. If a canonical rule badge for the reported field is retained, qualify its scope accordingly.
Remove or make unconditionally inert both memory forceStopFromMemory and safeDisableFromMemory paths, including the actual handlers. No force_stop or disable_package may be reached from these rows. Disable/omit controls with a visible inspect-only explanation; this applies to ALL current memory rows, including dotted-looking or known package names. No string allowlist, regex/prefix, or simple name match can prove installed ownership. Remove the immediate-RAM-free promise and riskLabel/catalog SAFE substitution. Failed/superseded safety lookups clear old readiness/badges and offer explicit retry; no new scan or sampling loop. Actual parser/process attribution remains the later .2 work.

OPTIMIZE TAB
Load canonical safety for actionable destructive plan items with per-request/plan/mode/serial/page-epoch guards. Starting a lookup clears old readiness. Unknown defaults to Skip despite default_optimize; explicit Disable/Uninstall overrides remain possible after valid lookup and a visible warning. Caution may retain a catalog default only after its valid verdict, with its consequence in confirmation. Protected/unavailable items cannot be made destructive by defaultAction, effectiveAction, actionOptions, setOptimizeAction, Run or direct function calls. Restore enable items remain usable without removal safety. Readiness must inspect every chosen destructive item, not only a batch loading flag. Preserve explicit user Skip choices when async verdicts arrive.
Stop calling Unknown removals recommended. When no actions are chosen, say none are selected; do not claim every item is already in its target state. Keep real purpose/name/description independently visible. Show canonical verdict/readiness in AppRow; remove the risk prop/display based on catalog risk from both its callers. Keep current filters and app layout otherwise.
executeOptimize captures an immutable array of package/action/verdict/reason entries plus plan/mode/serial/page-generation/resetToken BEFORE confirmation. Subsequent loop iterations must use that snapshot, never recalculate from mutable dropdowns or props. After confirmation and before each removal, recheck context, cancellation and a fresh canonical verdict; protected/unavailable/changed warnings stop further dispatch and require review. During the run, guard direct override/reload calls as well as controls. Observe resetToken/serial/context changes and destroy even when the tab is hidden; abort pending continuations and prevent stale result callbacks or finally blocks from clearing a newer run. Enable dispatch uses the captured current context too.
The existing separate performance button stays separate; it is not an automatic consequence of Unknown selection. Guard its captured context/result publication but do not change settings values or backend behavior. No broad optimize/performance redesign.

DEMO AND HANDOFF
Replace the all-Safe demo response with faithful representative Protected/Caution examples using exact existing core reasons for those fixtures and a valid Unknown reason fallback. These are synthetic fixture examples, not a second production classifier or review registry. Do not invent Optional provenance or change demo version/build metadata.
Return exact four-path before/after hashes and complete application diff, preservation evidence and source limitations. Mechanic owns actual-source isolated action/semantic checks in acceptance.txt; Navigator reviews the same frozen source/copy. Full frontend build/gallery waits for the host slot. Do not call this integrated, device-verified or released. After mobile+desktop acceptance, Mechanic assembles the staged contract and consumer deltas with focused combined gates; actual memory ownership and .6.1 typed local logging remain explicit follow-ups.

Mechanic scoped actual-source tests and Navigator source/copy acceptance; staged until combined migration checks.
notes: Navigator independent DESKTOP CONSUMER CONTRACT ACCEPTED at manifest0c94e70ddc1aa7649d00d15e5ea21edb6a6d081ca67be4f42af1056e61056a30 (hash verified). Read full four-path brief/12 acceptance cases and inspected original fetchAppStates/fallback/action references, AppRow and Optimize run/default references. Explicit inventory unavailable distinct from enabled/missing closes unsupported installation certainty; four catalog/Other removal handlers plus applyRecommendation require installed provenance, one captured confirmation and fresh canonical warning. Unknown neutral/explicit-only, known purpose separate, independent enable/reinstall and current supplied memory text inspect-only align with mobile contract. Frozen Optimize actions/context and canonical AppRow/demo avoid existing Safe overrides. No source/copy blocker or scope expansion requested. Implementation dependency remains accepted .2.2 via SAME serial helper; no concurrent editor. This is contract acceptance only, no candidate delta/test/integration acceptance; no edits/runtime/check execution. Mechanic owns frozen technical validation; gallery/full app/platform/device and actual memory attribution remain separate gates.

title: Migrate mobile app and memory actions to canonical Unknown safety
description:
so-fb3.2.2 — mobile consumers of the canonical Unknown contract

Next serial source slice for Flowkeeper's SAME Sol-high collaboration helper after exact so-fb3.2.1 contract acceptance. Mechanic owns technical acceptance and frozen-source harness; Navigator owns independent source/copy acceptance. No additional worker/session, clone/worktree, install, commit/push/release/device/network operation. No compiler/GUI/heavy frontend build by this implementer; return source for lead-owned scoped checks. Keep this capsule under 1 MiB.

BASELINE
manifest.json pins the current mechanic source at HEAD48cba2384ca3938e6655b77ccf85716dd86cca5f plus the actually integrated so-vtm.3/so-fb3.1.1 navigation/discovery foundation. The seven writable files are copied from that live baseline, including the already changed session.test.mjs; NEVER replace that test file from HEAD. ONLY these seven candidate/ paths are writable:
1. v2/mobile/src/lib/safety.ts
2. v2/mobile/src/components/AppDetailSheet.svelte
3. v2/mobile/src/screens/Apps.svelte
4. v2/mobile/src/screens/Diagnostics.svelte

Do not edit shared/safety.ts, types/API, session lifecycle, saved devices, desktop consumers, backend guards or the separate accepted Apps-filter/optional-review candidates. Report a concrete scope issue to Mayor/Flowkeeper if needed; do not expand scope silently.

VOCABULARY AND LOOKUP STATE
The actual shared union is NeverDisable(kind never_disable), Caution and Unknown, each with a reason. API boundary rejects failed/malformed/legacy Safe results. Display Protected, Caution and Unknown consistently. Unknown uses a neutral existing icon/color, never a green check. Pending means Checking safety; rejected/invalid means Safety unavailable with an explicit retry. Neither is a verdict or action-ready state. Do not fabricate Optional/review evidence from catalog risk="safe", known-names, app purpose, default flags or a device family. Preserve useful app names/purpose independently of uncertain removal impact: Unknown does not mean the app has no known purpose. Keep raw package/process text visible.
Update mobile lib/safety.ts to map the exact three kinds, return the backend reason for each, preserve isBlocked as the protected-only predicate (never mistake Unknown for an override), and make needsConfirm true for Caution AND Unknown. Callers must separately block absent verdicts. Remove the obsolete Safe descriptions and associated green styles in the six owned mobile files. RiskGuide must explain that known protection rules are mandatory but the classifier does not prove every other package safe. Do not promise that a mistap cannot harm a TV or that every uninstall can always be restored.

INSTALLED-APP DETAIL AND REMOVAL DISPATCH
Only an OtherPackage from the current, successfully loaded installed-app list can support a removal intent. Treat the list's serial, connection generation and local load/request token as part of its validity; a merely dotted string or old cached row is insufficient. Capture the existing session.generation getter and serial at load/request/confirmation boundaries. It is a plain getter, so an effect must also observe the existing reactive connectedDevice/liveness state; do not rely on that getter alone to trigger reruns. Invalidate pending lookups, old selection/confirmation and action readiness on load supersession, device switch, same-serial reconnect, disconnect or destroy. Preserve still-valid same-session rendering where useful, but stale data must be inert. Enrichment and action results may not publish back into a different session.

Use ONE confirmation owner in Apps.svelte for disable and uninstall. AppDetailSheet keeps immediate pending/protected/unavailable button guards and emits the existing action intent; remove its separate confirmDisable flow so it cannot confirm one package and later call onToggle for a different app. Parent handlers must enforce the same rules even when called directly, not merely rely on disabled buttons.
For a removal request, resolve the target from the valid current installed list, capture package/action/serial/generation/list token, call the canonical safetyInfo, and discard any stale completion. Protected refuses with its reason. Unavailable rejects with retry and no optimistic mutation. Unknown/Caution open the parent confirmation with the exact target, action and current reason; both need an explicit user confirmation. A cancel/close must discard the intent. Never recapture a new session or selected row as the target when confirming an old dialog.
At confirmation, revalidate the frozen intent and perform a fresh canonical lookup before dispatch. If the new verdict is protected/unavailable, abort. If kind or reason changed, require a new reviewable confirmation rather than acting under the previous warning. Only a matching still-current Unknown/Caution verdict and explicit confirmation may call disablePackage/uninstallPackage for the captured serial/package. Optimistic UI changes happen only after these checks. After await, apply results/errors/paywall/selection changes only while that action's captured session and token remain current. Preserve entitlement handling and the existing backend refusal; no override.
Enable/restore is not a removal action and does not wait on removal safety, but still needs a current target/session. Existing installed-app Force stop and other detail tools retain their behavior with current-target/session checks; do not add memory-process guesses to them. Preserve the existing post-uninstall Reinstall/Play Store behavior for the same session. Do not change the Apps filter, installed-storage/PSS model, icon system, or add new app-purpose data in this slice.

DIAGNOSTICS MEMORY ROWS
The current HealthReport MemoryEntry has only package:string and mb; the backend parser has not yet proved installed ownership and may truncate process names. This slice must therefore make ALL memory Disable and Force stop paths inspect-only. Remove their dispatchable callbacks/dialog or make the actual handlers refuse unconditionally as well as disabling the controls. No api.disablePackage/api.forceStop may be reachable from this screen's memory row. Do not gate only strings such as "system", infer validity from dots/colon prefixes, or borrow Apps inventory by a guessed name. A later .2 identity patch supplies actual unique installed ownership.
Show a concise visible explanation, for example "App identity is unverified. These memory entries are for inspection only." Keep measured PSS values and the reported token. If retaining a canonical rule badge for that token, qualify it as a lookup for the reported name, not proof that the process belongs to that installed app. Never turn an unresolved process into a known package by choosing a catalog label alone. Preserve useful catalog names as secondary descriptive hints only.
Clear old safety/name readiness when starting a superseding lookup or after a failure; include serial + session.generation + request guards and destroy invalidation. Show Checking/Unavailable separately and offer a retry using the existing lookup flow, without an automatic device scan. Remove the old promise that Force stop frees the process now. Do not change parser, health wire types, sampling interval or other diagnostics.

OPTIMIZE SELECTION, CONFIRMATION AND APPLY
Use canonical verdicts, never catalog risk, for removal selection/readiness/reason chips. Unknown destructive actions must start unchecked and have no Recommended badge or automatic recommendation, even when default_optimize is true. Caution may preserve an existing default selection only after its successful verdict is resolved, and the final confirmation must show its reason. Protected and unavailable destructive rows cannot be selected by toggle, Select all, or direct handler calls. Unknown may be explicitly selected from All curated/Select all, but requires the Unknown warning in the final dialog. Keep Unknown review choices discoverable: if the recommended subset is empty, explain it neutrally and offer All curated; do not claim everything is safe/optimized or silently hide all Unknown choices.
Restore enable actions remain selectable without a removal-safety lookup. Readiness must examine every selected destructive item, not only a batch-wide loading/failed boolean. Starting a lookup clears old readiness; a rejected batch cannot retain old verdicts. Remove the visible catalog:safe metadata from risk explanation; retain real name/description/purpose. Do not expand into performance/background-limit or paywall cleanup.
Guard prepareOptimize and safety responses with captured serial, session.generation, request token, mode and plan identity. notes:
Mechanic convoy triage 2026-09-06: #87 Sony Android 8 reports enabled Projectivy failed but disable then Enable & Set Default succeeded. Current launcher.rs stock fast path only tries cmd package set-home-activity for a discovered component before disabling/reverting stock; the later full ladder tries both cmd package and pm set-home-activity, but a stock-takeover failure returns early. This compatibility asymmetry is a concrete candidate for mock regression/repair; actual Sony output is unavailable. Never add automatic disable/re-enable of target as workaround or weaken never-disable/opt-in/rollback gates. Ready for focused core launcher worker once a slot frees; no overlap with current desktop driver/mobile integration owners.
Follow-up source validation: AOSP Android 8.0.0_r4 PackageManagerShellCommand supports set-home-activity, so a blanket assumption that Android 8 lacks cmd package is incorrect. Source https://android.googlesource.com/platform/frameworks/base/+/android-8.0.0_r4/services/core/java/com/android/server/pm/PackageManagerShellCommand.java . Stock-fast-path asymmetry alone does not prove Sony root cause; do not implement speculative pm fallback as a claimed fix. Need evidence-based controlled regression/diagnostic or actual device command results. Newly confirmed #88 hard-coded post-pair 5555 defect takes priority.
Current disposition after full source/AOSP review: no evidence-backed Sony-specific production repair established. Exact failing stage is stock takeover confirmation after rollback; pm/cmd API presence asymmetry is not sufficient root-cause proof, and reported disable-target/enable workaround must not be automated. Remaining gate: owner/reporter reproduction with selected launcher enabled state, actual resolve-activity/HOME component and setter command result across failure/success, with explicit device authorization. No device mutation performed. Continue independent ready tasks; external #87 remains unresolved, not implemented.
Navigator independent read-only trace at application HEAD 48cba2384ca3938e6655b77ccf85716dd86cca5f: the enabled Set as default and disabled Enable & set default controls differ only in label/title and both call the same setDefaultLauncher(package) frontend callback. The backend always issues pm enable target first and ignores its result. Thus the only source-provable behavioral difference is pre-call package state: for a disabled target pm enable is a real PackageManager transition that can change HOME resolution before the next active-launcher query or verifier; for an already-enabled target it is normally a no-op and stock can remain active, entering stock fast-path/takeover. The exact issue error is constructed only after stock disable reports success, HOME intent runs, and three resolver polls totaling about 1.6s never report target; code then best-effort re-enables stock but does not check rollback output or freshly resolve returned state. This maps the user-visible failure to takeover verification plus assumed rollback, not to either frontend button. It does not prove whether Sony HOME resolution was delayed/stale or enable transition repaired device state. Acceptance evidence should record initial target enabled state/current HOME, pm enable result, discovered target activity, role/set-home acknowledgements, every resolver result/timing, stock disable result, and verified rollback state. Focused regression should cover identical Sony-like resolver sequences from initially enabled and disabled targets; surface enable failure, accept a post-enable target resolution as success, use a fresh final verification before rollback, and report rollback failure distinctly. Do not automate disable/re-enable of target or weaken stock opt-in/safety gates.
Navigator contract follow-up ACCEPTED for launcher.rs-only failure handling. Additional exact source defect confirmed: disabled_ok false falls through to the same Disabled stock ... re-enabled message even though no rollback ran; when disable succeeded but takeover did not verify, rollback pm enable output is ignored. Both branches return current_launcher=the pre-attempt stock package without a final resolver observation. Initial target pm enable is also ignored, so stock removal may be offered/executed after target enable failure. Copy must be outcome-specific: target enable failure says target could not be enabled and stock was not disabled; stock-disable failure says stock could not be disabled and must not claim rollback; unverified takeover plus acknowledged rollback may say switch was not verified and stock was re-enabled, but may call stock active only after a fresh resolver; rollback failure/unknown must say current HOME could not be confirmed and direct the user to Refresh/TV Settings or recovery without asserting a launcher. Capture the actual command error safely in each case. Progress should say Restoring the stock launcher during rollback. Preserve frontend verbatim rendering and final reload, explicit stock opt-in, NEVER_DISABLE gate, stock-only target, mandatory rollback attempt, and no automated target toggle. Tests need transport and shell-reported failure for initial enable, stock disable, and rollback; delayed/none/unexpected final resolver; and exact no-false-verb/current_launcher assertions. This improves truthful handling of the reported path without claiming Sony root cause.
CORRECTION superseding the earlier Navigator sentence that mapped the exact reporter text exclusively to successful stock disable plus failed verification: launcher.rs disabled_ok=false skips HOME intent, verification and rollback, then falls through to the identical Disabled stock ... re-enabled message. Therefore the observed text proves neither that stock disable succeeded nor that rollback ran. It has two source paths: (A) stock disable transport/shell-reported failure with no HOME kick, verifier or rollback; (B) stock disable success followed by unverified target and a best-effort rollback whose outcome is ignored. Branch-specific result/copy plus final resolver evidence is required to distinguish them. The identical frontend controls and target-enable state-transition possibility remain valid, but are not Sony causality.
